name: Muc mot nang
summary: Tube squid, split and dried one sun on a grid, so the outside dries and the inside stays raw. Grill it on the island or carry it home. The 2014 note gives two seasons. Confirm they still hold. No stall price was printed.
origin: Cham Islands. Tube squid, mực ống, split, cleaned of the gut and the ink sac, rinsed in seawater, and pinned at the fins.
culture: The 7 July 2014 heritage note says visitors eat this squid on the island and carry it home as a gift. The 15 September 2025 study still lists dried squid among the island’s dried seafood.
texture: It is dried one sun on a grid so the outside dries and the inside stays raw. The 2014 note says mực lá, mực cơm, and mực ghim are not the squid they dry, and that the smallest grade is eaten fresh.
howToEat: Grill it, or take it as the gift the 2014 page describes.

On that 2014 note the main seasons were vụ Nam, June to September, and vụ Bắc, December to April. Winter drying then used squid bought off Quảng Ngãi boats and was not as good. Confirm the seasons on the boat day.
where: Bai Lang. No shop was named on the heritage pages.
seoTitle: Muc mot nang — squid dried one sun, Cham Islands
seoDescription: Tube squid dried one sun on Cù Lao Chàm, so the outside dries and the inside stays raw. Grill it or carry it home. The price is check on arrival.
